editable_notice: EDITABLE STARTER SAMPLE RULES ONLY. Replace, remove, or expand these entries with reviewed sources and local policy before relying on reports.

rules.meaning: Often used in white supremacist spaces by combining references to the '14 words' slogan and '88' as a coded reference to HH.
rules.context_note: Can appear in unrelated usernames, dates, gamer tags, or OCR errors; surrounding profile text and repeated signals matter.
rules.review_guidance: Check whether the number appears with ideology-linked slogans, symbols, account follows, or repeated use across screenshots.

rules.meaning: Sometimes used as coded shorthand for HH in extremist contexts.
rules.context_note: Very ambiguous by itself because it can indicate a birth year, jersey number, address, price, or ordinary handle text.
rules.review_guidance: Treat as weak evidence unless it repeats or appears near clearer slogans, symbols, or ideological references.

rules.meaning: A slogan historically associated with ethno-nationalist and Nazi propaganda.
rules.context_note: Could appear in historical criticism, quotation, documentation, satire, or news discussion.
rules.review_guidance: Look for whether the phrase is endorsed, quoted critically, or surrounded by other ideological signals.

rules.meaning: A symbol reference used in some neo-Nazi and white supremacist contexts.
rules.context_note: The words can also appear in art, music, history, gaming, or anti-extremism discussion.
rules.review_guidance: Review whether the reference is a visual symbol, an aesthetic phrase, or a critical discussion.

rules.meaning: A swastika can be used as a Nazi or neo-Nazi symbol in extremist contexts.
rules.context_note: The symbol can also appear in historical documentation, anti-extremism reporting, religious contexts, satire, or opposition speech.
rules.review_guidance: Confirm the visual context, orientation, accompanying text, and whether it is displayed approvingly or critically.

rules.meaning: The Confederate battle flag is used in some racist, white supremacist, and anti-government contexts.
rules.context_note: It can also appear in history, regional identity, criticism, documentary material, or counter-speech; it is not conclusive by itself.
rules.review_guidance: Look for whether it is paired with racist slogans, other extremist symbols, threats, or repeated ideological signals.

rules.meaning: SS bolt imagery is associated with Nazi and neo-Nazi symbolism.
rules.context_note: Lightning-like graphics can be ordinary branding, music imagery, sports design, or OCR/visual-review error.
rules.review_guidance: Check whether the shape clearly resembles SS bolts and whether it appears with other Nazi-linked references.

rules.meaning: Totenkopf or death's-head imagery can reference Nazi SS symbolism in extremist contexts.
rules.context_note: Skull imagery is common in fashion, motorcycles, music, games, military history, and tattoo art.
rules.review_guidance: Review the exact design and surrounding account context before treating it as a meaningful signal.

rules.meaning: The OK hand gesture has been used as a trolling or extremist signal in some contexts.
rules.context_note: It is extremely ambiguous and commonly means OK, approval, diving signal, game gesture, or ordinary posing.
rules.review_guidance: Treat as weak evidence unless repeated or paired with clearer extremist symbols, slogans, or account references.

rules.meaning: A Nazi salute or similar raised-arm gesture can indicate extremist signaling when used approvingly.
rules.context_note: Still images can mislead; raised arms can be waving, dancing, pointing, performance, parody, or historical depiction.
rules.review_guidance: Check sequence context if available, caption text, repetition, and whether the gesture is endorsed or criticized.

rules.meaning: A tattoo resembling an extremist symbol can be a relevant visual signal when the design is identifiable.
rules.context_note: Tattoos are easy to misread from screenshots, can be cover-ups, art, music references, or unrelated designs.
rules.review_guidance: Document the visible design carefully, avoid guessing, and seek corroborating context before relying on it.

rules.meaning: A violent extremist phrase from white supremacist fiction and propaganda.
rules.context_note: May appear in reporting, research, fiction analysis, or condemnation rather than endorsement.
rules.review_guidance: Escalate for careful human review if presented approvingly or paired with threats, targets, or repeated extremist references.

rules.meaning: A reference associated with a white power band and related music scenes.
rules.context_note: Could be a music-history reference, typo, quotation, or critical discussion.
rules.review_guidance: Check whether the account appears to promote the reference, simply mention it, or discuss it critically.

rules.meaning: A reference associated with a far-right online subculture.
rules.context_note: Meaning depends heavily on community, meme use, criticism, and surrounding political context.
rules.review_guidance: Look for repeated subculture references, linked accounts, memes, and whether the term is self-identification or commentary.
